correctness.rationale: For n>=3 every edge has at least one split side of size >=2, so the normalized curvature H(q)=n(n−1)L−sum_e ℓ_e[a(a−1)q^(−b)+b(b−1)q^(−a)] is continuous, strictly increasing on (0,1), diverges to −∞ at zero, and is 2 sum_e ℓ_e ab>0 at one. Thus U has one sign reversal. Bernoulli q0=(n−2)/n gives each split contribution >=n(n−1), with strictness precisely at nonpendant edges, proving 0<p_T<=2/n and star equality. Conditional Jensen and rooted PD second derivative prove the environmental signs. Exact subset-enumeration program verifies 8 finite cases without being used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The missing curvature structure is ecologically motivated: expected unrooted evolutionary history is a nonlinear function of common survival probability. The result establishes a universal and unique change of curvature for every tree with a sharp 2/n bound and exact star extremizer, and distinguishes beneficial vs harmful effects of shared environmental variance at fixed marginal survival. It gives a structural classification and applicable sign comparison, not a textbook first derivative, isolated example or arbitrary parameter slice.
